The motivation is that most contact-map methods rely on multiple-sequence-alignment (MSA) and evolutionary-profile information, which may not exist for many proteins lacking homologous sequences, and generating such profiles is computationally intensive. The authors argue that a method using only single-sequence features plus transformer-derived features can provide a faster, reasonably accurate alternative for large-scale prediction. Methodologically, they curated a dataset from ProteinNet (50914 proteins submitted to PDB before 2016 with high-resolution crystal structures), clustered at 95% sequence identity, then removed homologs via HHblits (e-value < 0.1) to obtain a training set of 34691 proteins and a validation set of 88 proteins. Independent test sets include SPOT-2018 (669 proteins), Neff1-2018 (46 proteins with Neff=1), and CASP14-FM (15 free-modeling targets). The neural network architecture is a 12-block ResNet (using an improved ResNet variant from Duta et al., 2020), with six models trained on different feature combinations (attention map from last layer vs. all layers, direct contact prediction vs. distance-bin prediction), using Adam optimizer (learning rate 0.001, batch size 1), early stopping of 3, Binary Cross-Entropy loss for direct prediction and Cross-Entropy loss for distogram-based prediction. Contact definition follows CASP: inter-residue distance ≤ 8.0 Å between Cβ atoms, classified into long (≥24 residues), medium (12-23), and short (7-11) ranges. Key results show a 15% improvement in F1-score over SSCpred on CASP14-FM, and 48.7% and 48.5% improvement over TrRosetta and SPOT-Contact on proteins without homologs (Neff=1) in SPOT-2018. Feature importance analysis shows one-hot encoding alone yields F1=0.15, SPOT-1D-Single improves F1 by 22.90%, and ESM-1b attention maps (last layer) yield F1=0.51, MCC=0.50, precision=0.56, AUC=0.95, with 242% and 178% improvement over one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single+one-hot encoding respectively. The ensemble (SPOT-Contact-Single) shows 4% improvement over the second-best individual model on validation. On CASP14-FM, SPOT-Contact-Single achieves F1=0.2061, MCC=0.1925, and is 45% higher F1 (0.32) than evolution-based methods on Neff=1 proteins. Computational efficiency: SPOT-Contact-Single runs in 116 seconds on CPU (22x faster than TrRosetta) and is 42x faster on GPU. Limitations include inability to predict proteins with more than 1024 amino acids due to ESM-1b attention map constraints. The paper contributes a fast, single-sequence-based method that performs competitively with evolution-based methods for proteins lacking homologs, with implications for large-scale and de-novo protein structure prediction.
